acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce or refute the reported cancelled work-state tick at the exact current source/runtime; retain prior main-25ba271 and 365-ticket/704-event evidence without calling it a fresh run.
Shutdown cancellation stops the current tick before applying UNKNOWN work states or publishing per-ticket transitions, while genuine reader failures retain useful explicit diagnostics.

Regression distinguishes shutdown cancellation from a real UNKNOWN work-state change and verifies interruption retires owned descendants; retain focused checks, independent review, CEM/OCM, integration and native completion.
body:
Owning GitHub issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/464 (reported against main-25ba271). Reporter evidence and requested behavior:

## Problem

`corvint-tasks dispatch` (`main-25ba271`, workState kind `command`): when the dispatcher receives SIGTERM while the work-state command is running, the command's context is cancelled. The tick still continues with every ticket's work state set to `UNKNOWN`. On the next start, every ticket flips back.

Observed 2026-10-01 at 23:04Z on a 365-ticket queue:

```
alert   work state command: context canceled
state   MX-5 changed: status OPEN→OPEN, work state NONE→UNKNOWN, plan BLOCKED (...)→BLOCKED (...)
...     (one line per ticket)
stopped dispatcher stopped; 2 worker(s) left running for the next dispatcher
started ...
state   MX-5 changed: ... work state UNKNOWN→NONE ...
```

In total there were 704 spurious "state changed" events in `events.jsonl` from one restart. They drown real transitions for subscribers such as our timeline and notifier.

## Request

When the dispatcher is shutting down (context cancelled), skip the rest of the tick: don't apply `UNKNOWN` states and don't emit change events. More generally, consider not emitting per-ticket `state` events when the only change is the work state moving into or out of `UNKNOWN` because of a reader failure; one `alert` line is enough.
